reviews.evidence: Lev.7.1-6 is framed by וְזֹאת תּוֹרַת הָאָשָׁם and closes its procedure, while 7.7 begins the comparative כַּחַטָּאת כָּאָשָׁם תּוֹרָה אַחַת and 7.7-10 reallocates portions across three offerings; translating חטאת as purification offering and אשם as reparation offering makes the functional change clearer.
reviews.counterevidence: MT/OSHB has no open or closed parashah marker before 7.7, and 7.7 deliberately links the reparation offering back to the preceding procedure.
reviews.remedy: Split into M7_sol-Lev-012a Lev.7.1-6 and M7_sol-Lev-012b Lev.7.7-10, preserving their parent and the existing cross-offering links.

reviews.evidence: וַיְהִי בַּיּוֹם הַשְּׁמִינִי opens one command-execution-result narrative culminating in כְבוֹד־יְהוָה and fire at 9.23-24; English offering terminology may vary but does not create a seam.
reviews.counterevidence: The commands at 9.1-7, execution at 9.8-21, and blessing/glory at 9.22-24 are valid internal stages.
reviews.remedy: Retain Lev.9.1-24 and record 9.1-7, 9.8-21, and 9.22-24 only as internal stages.

reviews.evidence: The Sabbath provision closes at 23.3 with an OSHB פ marker, and 23.4 restarts with אֵלֶּה מוֹעֲדֵי יְהוָה; rendering מועדים as appointed times rather than merely feasts preserves the relation without erasing the seam.
reviews.counterevidence: The similar headings in 23.2 and 23.4 show that the Sabbath remains conceptually inside the chapter-wide appointed-times corpus.
reviews.remedy: Retain Lev.23.1-3 under the required Lev.23.1-44 parent.

reviews.evidence: אֵלֶּה מוֹעֲדֵי at 23.4 opens the dated annual sequence, Passover and Unleavened Bread form its coordinated first-month opening, and an OSHB ס marker closes 23.8.
reviews.counterevidence: Passover at 23.5 and Unleavened Bread at 23.6-8 are distinguishable observances and could be represented as internal subunits.
reviews.remedy: Retain Lev.23.4-8; do not create a one-verse Passover child.

reviews.evidence: A fresh וַיְדַבֵּר speech supplies date, זִכְרוֹן תְּרוּעָה, convocation, work prohibition, and offering, then closes with OSHB ס; the phrase may mean memorial of a blast rather than explicitly trumpets.
reviews.counterevidence: Three verses are short and remain closely related to the following seventh-month observance.
reviews.remedy: Retain Lev.23.23-25 as a short structurally closed child under the calendar parent.

reviews.evidence: Lev.23.26 begins a fresh וַיְדַבֵּר speech, 23.27 introduces a new date with emphatic אַךְ, and 23.32 closes the observance with שַׁבַּת שַׁבָּתוֹן and evening bounds; ענה נפש permits translation variation without weakening the seam.
reviews.counterevidence: Its seventh-month placement and repeated rest vocabulary bind it closely to Lev.23.23-25 and the full festival calendar.
reviews.remedy: Retain Lev.23.26-32 with links to Lev.16.29-34 and the Lev.23 parent.

reviews.evidence: After the OSHB ס at 24.9, וַיֵּצֵא opens the case whose custody, divine ruling, generalized law, and execution resolve together at 24.23; נקב and קלל support translation caution around blaspheming or pronouncing the Name but not a boundary change.
reviews.counterevidence: Lev.24.10-12, 13-22, and 23 are clear narrative, ruling, and execution stages.
reviews.remedy: Retain Lev.24.10-23 and preserve the three stages as an internal map.

reviews.evidence: An OSHB ס closes the apodictic allegiance commands at 26.2, while 26.3 begins a formal אִם protasis followed by blessing clauses from 26.4, making 26.3 the Hebrew structural opening of the blessings.
reviews.counterevidence: Lev.26.1-2 supplies the allegiance frame for the conditional blessings, and a two-verse child risks overfragmentation.
reviews.remedy: Split into M7_sol-Lev-061a Lev.26.1-2 and M7_sol-Lev-061b Lev.26.3-13, retain both under Lev.25.1-26.46, and keep the short first child flagged for human review.

external_corpus_gap: No reviewed ANE, Second Temple, ancient Jewish, or rabbinic corpus was available; none was simulated.
